masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A carved wooden two-piece ceremonial mask with painted facial features and fur eyebrows, consistent with Northwest Coast Nuxalk mask-making traditions, with the museum explicitly attributing it as made by the Nuxalk.

masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: A painted wooden human face mask with cedar-bark fiber hair, attributed by the museum directly to Nuxalk makers; this type of carved ceremonial mask is well documented among Nuxalk/Northwest Coast dance traditions.

photo.name: photographic print; carte-de-visite
photo.title: photographic print (black and white); carte-de-visite
photo.reason: Studio portrait (carte-de-visite) of a named Nuxalk man, Tom Henry, wearing a Chilkat-style blanket, fur hat and face paint — genuine Northwest Coast regalia documented on an actual Indigenous sitter, even though the photo was taken in Hamburg (likely for a touring exhibition). This counts as a documentary photo of dress regardless of where it was shot.
